ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the circuit is power supply E, and the right side is lamp F. Above there are two branch circuits connecting the same left and right nodes: the upper branch has only one switch A; the lower branch passes through switch B and switch C in sequence, so B and C are in series on the same branch. The upper and lower two branches are connected between the same pair of nodes, so branch A and the B-C series branch are in parallel. Reasoning: The problem stipulates that switch closed/on is recorded as 1, and open/off is recorded as 0; lamp on is recorded as F=1. The series branch must have both B and C as 1 to conduct, corresponding to logical multiplication BC. For the parallel branches, as long as A conducts, or the B-C series branch conducts, the lamp will light, corresponding to logical addition. Therefore the logic function is F = A + BC.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure: switch A is on the upper branch by itself, while switches B and C lie on a second branch connected between the same two nodes, so B and C are in series and that series branch is in parallel with A. From the text, take closed/on switch as 1 and lamp on as F=1. Convert the B-C series branch to BC, then OR it with the parallel A branch, giving F = A + BC.
